title: Record reuse
summary: Shows how to prove the compiler's in-place rewrite of a consumed record: in the record branch of a match on an owned value, a constructor of the same type stores each changed field into the matched record's slot and returns the record's pointer.
premises: A consumed argument of type Moved α, whose Represent instance gives NodeOwned and pairwise disjoint blocks
Heap.At, whose top bounds the record's slots inside memory
The rewritten slot holds a word
result: The write changes only the slot's bytes, the allocator invariant holds, the record holds the new word with the same header and blocks, every array apart from the consumed records keeps its contents, and the result's blocks are the consumed blocks.
